# 1 Clement Chapter 43 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 43 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_043_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 43

**43:1** Is it any surprise, then, that those who were entrusted with such a great work in Christ sent forward people of this caliber — when even the blessed Moses, described as "a faithful servant in all his house," wrote down in the holy scriptures everything that had been commanded to him?

**43:2** After him came the other prophets, all bearing witness to the laws he had given.

**43:3** When rivalry broke out over the priesthood, and the tribes started arguing among themselves about which one should bear the glorious name, Moses commanded the twelve tribal leaders to bring him staffs with each tribe's name written on it. He took the staffs, bound and sealed them with each leader's ring, and placed them on the table of God inside the Tent of Meeting.

**43:4** He then shut the Tent and sealed the keys the same way he had sealed the staffs.

**43:5** And he said: "Brothers, the tribe whose staff blossoms — that is the tribe God has chosen to serve him as priests."

**43:6** Early the next morning, he assembled all Israel — six hundred thousand men — showed them the seals, opened the Tent of Meeting, and brought out the staffs. And Aaron's staff had not only blossomed — it was bearing fruit.

**43:7** What do you make of that, dear friends? Did Moses not already know what was going to happen? Of course he did. But he did all this so that there would be no disorder in Israel, and so that the name of the true and only God would be glorified — to whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen.

---

*PNEUMA renders the Aaron's rod narrative with narrative momentum and clarity, making the typological point (divine validation of legitimate leadership against rivals) readily accessible.*
